page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What MRI uses
steps.why: Magnetism and radio waves do not break chemical bonds, so they do not damage cells the way X-rays can.
common_mistakes: Saying MRI uses a small amount of X-rays. It uses none.
steps.memory_tip: Magnets and radio waves — no ionising radiation.
steps.margin_note: Say what it uses before saying why it is safe.
lines: It uses magnetism, radio waves and a computer

steps.label: Why it is safe
steps.why: Ionising radiation is what makes X-rays risky, and MRI does not produce any.
common_mistakes: Ending without the conclusion. The question says justify.
Giving a reason unrelated to radiation.
steps.memory_tip: No ionising radiation means no radiation risk.
lines: MRI does not use ionising radiation as used

lines.text: So MRI scanning is a very safe procedure

insider_note: A justify question needs a reason, not a description. The reason is that MRI uses no ionising radiation.
